# DSP Architecture: O-simplePhysicalModelSynth

**CRITICAL CONTRACT:** This specification is immutable during Stages 1-4 implementation. Stage 1 Planning cannot proceed without this file. Stage 2 (DSP) implements this exact architecture.

**Generated by:** Stage 0 Research (research-planning-agent)
**Date:** 2026-06-26
**Referenced by:** Stage 1 (Foundation), Stage 2 (DSP Implementation), Stage 3 (GUI)
**Purpose:** DSP specification for a pedagogical physical-modeling synth — the teaching distillation of O-Lyrica (KS string), O-Bells (modal), and O-Bowed (waveguide/friction), structured like O-simpleFM / O-simpleAdditive.

**Plugin type:** Instrument (synth) — `IS_SYNTH TRUE`, MIDI-in / audio-out, 16-voice polyphonic. WebView UI.

**Unifying mental model (the whole point):** `EXCITATION → RESONATOR → MATERIAL/DAMPING`. One chain; the resonator switches between **String** (Karplus-Strong) and **Modal** (resonant bank). The same three exciters (Pluck / Strike / Bow) drive either resonator.

---

## Research Summary — Resolved Open Questions

The 8 "Research Must Confirm" items from `parameter-spec-draft.md`, resolved against the in-house production models. These decisions are binding for Stage 2.

| # | Open question | Resolution |
|---|---------------|-----------|
| 1 | Fractional-delay tuning method | **First-order all-pass fractional delay** via `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float, Thiran>` (Thiran 1st-order IS an all-pass interpolator — validated in O-Bowed). Loop-filter group delay is compensated out of the integer delay length (O-Lyrica `calculateFilterGroupDelay` pattern). Pitch fixed per note at trigger → Thiran's "no fast modulation" caveat does not apply (no glide in v1.0). Satisfies DSP-02. |
| 2 | Modal mode count + default mode sets | **N = 8 modes** (matches O-Bells `NUM_PARTIALS`; keeps the stem display legible; 8 modes × 16 voices = 128 resonators, trivially affordable per O-Bassoon precedent). Mode frequencies via the **textbook stretched-partial formula `f_k = f0·k·√(1 + B·k²)`** (Fletcher inharmonicity), `B` driven by the Inharmonicity knob: `B=0` → perfectly harmonic (bar-like / near-marimba); higher `B` → stretched inharmonic (bell-like). Per-mode decay multipliers (higher modes decay faster) reuse O-Bells `DECAY_MULTIPLIERS`. Satisfies DSP-04, DSP-05. |
| 3 | Material macro curve | Single steel↔nylon axis co-moves (Damping cutoff, Decay feedback). **Steel** = bright loop LPF (~10 kHz) + long feedback (g≈0.995). **Nylon** = dark loop LPF (~2 kHz) + shorter feedback (g≈0.93). Cutoff interpolated in **log-frequency**, feedback **linearly**, along `material∈[0,1]` (0 = steel, 100 = nylon; default 30 = steel-ish). The macro **writes** the Damping + Decay parameter values so both visible knobs move with it (the demo's one-gesture sweep). Satisfies DSP-07. |
| 4 | Excitation design (DC-safe, stable Bow) | **Pluck** = short filtered noise burst + brightness LPF + position comb (O-Lyrica `PluckExciter` pattern). **Strike** = short raised-cosine-windowed band-limited impulse / mallet (O-Bells `StrikeExciter` pattern — NOT a single unit sample → no DC/alias click). **Bow** = STK-style **memoryless bow-table friction** driving the string junction (sustained), and a sustained filtered friction-noise drive into the modal bank. DC-blocker on the exciter sum. Satisfies DSP-08, QUAL-01. |
| 5 | Waveguide-vs-KS string scope | **Karplus-Strong is the v1.0 String engine (must, DSP-01).** Excitation Position is realised in v1.0 by a **feed-forward comb on the KS exciter** (O-Lyrica `PluckExciter` already does exactly this — position-dependent spectral nulls). The dual-delay **Waveguide** (true traveling-wave rails + physical pickup) is a **`nice`-tier Stage 2 phase (DSP-06)**, reusing O-Lyrica/O-Bowed `WaveguideString`; deferred if time-constrained without blocking v1.0. |
| 6 | Polyphony | **Confirmed 16 voices** (`juce::Synthesiser`, matches O-simpleFM / O-simpleAdditive). |
| 7 | Visualization tap | **Single GLOBAL tap following the LEAD voice** (most-recently-triggered) — NOT per-voice. One readable model is the pedagogy (mirrors O-simpleSubtractive's lead-voice display pattern). Scope/spectrum via the O-simpleFM `VizRing` lock-free ring (audio-thread copy-only); loop-energy scalar + modal-stem array via relaxed atomics. Satisfies UI-02, PERF-01. |
| 8 | Bow second control | **NO second Bow control in v1.0.** `bowForce` is the single Bow parameter — keep the irreducible teaching control set. A "Bow Speed" knob is documented as a v1.1 nice-to-have. |

## Core Components

### 1. KS String Resonator (primary String engine)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom `StringResonator` built on `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float, juce::dsp::DelayLineInterpolationTypes::Thiran>` + a custom one-pole loop LPF (O-Lyrica `OnePoleLPF` POD struct).
- **Purpose:** The canonical Karplus-Strong loop — excitation written once into an N-sample delay; each pass the oldest sample is output and `feedback × loopLPF(sample)` is written back. The two-tap-average → one-pole LPF is the class's derived loop filter.
- **Parameters Affected:** `damping` (loop LPF cutoff), `decay` (feedback gain), `coarseTune`, `fineTune`, `excitationPosition` (via exciter comb).
- **Configuration:**
  - Delay length `N = sampleRate / f0 − loopFilterGroupDelay − allpassPhaseDelay`; fractional remainder handled by the Thiran interpolator.
  - Pitch `f0` from MIDI note × 2^((coarse + fine/100)/12).
  - Loop: `y[n] = delay.popSample(); s = loopLPF(y[n]); delay.pushSample(feedback * s + exciter[n])`.
  - `feedback` (Decay) hard-clamped to `[0.80, 0.999]` (< 1, QUAL-01/DSP-03).
  - DC-blocker on output (`y[n] − y[n−1] + 0.995·dc[n−1]`).

### 2. Fractional-Delay Tuning (all-pass interpolation)
- **JUCE Class:** Built into `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float, Thiran>` (1st-order Thiran = all-pass fractional delay).
- **Purpose:** Keep notes in tune across the keyboard — integer-only delay quantizes pitch and goes audibly sharp/flat at high notes (DSP-02).
- **Parameters Affected:** all pitch params; implicit.
- **Configuration:** Set `delay.setDelay(fractionalN)`; recompute group-delay compensation when `damping` changes the loop LPF (O-Lyrica `calculateFilterGroupDelay`). Validated by the Stage-2 autocorrelation pitch probe (within a few cents, C1–C7).

### 3. Loop Damping Filter + Feedback (Material/Damping core)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom one-pole LPF (`OnePoleLPF`, bilinear-transform coeffs) + scalar feedback gain.
- **Purpose:** The two numbers the class says set the result — Damping darkens a little each pass (bright steel ↔ muted nylon); Decay (feedback) sets ring time.
- **Parameters Affected:** `damping`, `decay`, `material` (macro).
- **Configuration:**
  - `damping` (0–100%) → loop LPF cutoff, log-mapped ~1.5 kHz (dark) … ~12 kHz (bright).
  - `decay` (0–100%) → feedback gain `g = lerp(0.80, 0.999, decay/100)`, **clamped < 1**.
  - Coefficient changes crossfaded over ~64 samples to avoid zipper clicks (O-Lyrica shadow-filter pattern).

### 4. Waveguide String (`nice` — DSP-06, deferred-capable)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom `WaveguideString` — dual `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float, Thiran>` rails (upper/lower), bridge LPF, nut sign-inversion. Direct reuse of O-Lyrica / O-Bowed `WaveguideString`.
- **Purpose:** Two traveling-wave delays reflecting at each end — makes Excitation Position physically meaningful (true pickup point) and enables the traveling-wave viz skin.
- **Parameters Affected:** `excitationPosition`, `damping`, `decay`, plus the String/Waveguide `stringModel` switch.
- **Configuration:** Each rail = half the round-trip delay; injection split at the contact point set by `excitationPosition`. Only built if the `nice` phase ships; otherwise `stringModel` exposes KS only.

### 5. Modal Resonator Bank
- **JUCE Class:** Custom direct-form **resonant bandpass biquad bank** (8 modes), per O-Bassoon precedent (custom arrays, NOT `juce::dsp::IIR::Filter` at 16-voice scale).
- **Purpose:** A struck/plucked/bowed body — a parallel bank of damped harmonic oscillators **driven by the same exciter signal** (so any exciter rings it; FUNC-04). Impulse → rings; noise burst → rings; sustained bow noise → sustains.
- **Parameters Affected:** `inharmonicity`, `modeBrightness`, `damping`, `decay`, `material`.
- **Configuration:**
  - Mode `k` (1..8): center `f_k = f0·k·√(1 + B·k²)`; `B` from `inharmonicity`.
  - Q from per-mode T60: `Q_k = π·f_k·T60_k / sampleRate`-equivalent; `T60_k` scaled by `decay` and O-Bells `DECAY_MULTIPLIERS[k]` (higher modes faster).
  - Gain tilt: upper-mode amplitude falls with `k`; `modeBrightness` raises the tilt (brighter/metallic). `damping` applies an additional global HF gain rolloff.
  - Excited by the exciter sample fed in parallel to all 8 bandpass filters; outputs summed.

### 6. Inharmonicity Model
- **JUCE Class:** Inline math in the modal bank (no separate class).
- **Purpose:** Stretch mode spacing from harmonic (bar) → inharmonic (bell) — the defining modal control (DSP-05).
- **Parameters Affected:** `inharmonicity`.
- **Configuration:** `B = (inharmonicity/100)·B_max` (B_max ≈ 0.012, tuned so 100% reads clearly bell-like). Recomputed at note-on and on knob change (block rate). The stem display reads these `f_k` directly.

### 7. Pluck Exciter (noise burst)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom `PluckExciter` — `juce::Random` noise + `juce::ADSR` (or short ramp) + brightness LPF (`OnePoleLPF`) + feed-forward position comb. Direct O-Lyrica pattern.
- **Purpose:** Canonical KS exciter — a short broadband noise burst.
- **Parameters Affected:** `excitationColor`, `excitationPosition`, `velToBrightness`, velocity.
- **Configuration:** Burst length ~5–15 ms; brightness LPF cutoff from `excitationColor` (+ velocity via `velToBrightness`); position comb `y[n] = x[n] − x[n − D]`, `D = position·period`.

### 8. Strike Exciter (impulse / mallet)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom `StrikeExciter` — band-limited impulse (raised-cosine window, a few samples) + hardness LPF. O-Bells `StrikeExciter` pattern.
- **Purpose:** Struck strings and the natural exciter for the modal body — a short filtered mallet hit.
- **Parameters Affected:** `excitationColor` (mallet hardness), `excitationPosition`, `velToBrightness`, velocity.
- **Configuration:** Raised-cosine impulse (NOT a single unit sample → no DC/alias click); width and LPF cutoff from `excitationColor` (soft mallet ↔ hard).

### 9. Bow Exciter (sustained friction)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom `BowExciter` — STK-style **memoryless bow-table friction** for the String junction; sustained filtered friction-noise for the Modal bank.
- **Purpose:** Continuous stick-slip drive that **sustains** the note instead of letting it decay (FUNC-02 acceptance: Bow does not decay while held).
- **Parameters Affected:** `bowForce`, `velToBrightness`, velocity.
- **Configuration:** String: bow velocity vs string junction velocity → memoryless friction curve (STK `BowTable`), output injected each sample; `bowForce` scales the friction pressure / curve sharpness. Modal: sustained band-limited friction noise at level = `bowForce`. **Tiered** (core = memoryless; the elasto-plastic/NR-solved tier is OUT OF SCOPE — O-Bowed memory: friction is the highest-risk component, always memoryless-first). Active only while note held; clamps prevent blow-up.

### 10. Material Macro Mapping
- **JUCE Class:** Inline parameter mapping in the processor (writes `damping` + `decay` targets).
- **Purpose:** One-knob steel↔nylon convenience that co-moves Damping + Decay (DSP-07).
- **Parameters Affected:** `material` → drives `damping`, `decay`.
- **Configuration:** See Open Q3 — log-frequency cutoff lerp + linear feedback lerp along `material`.

### 11. Velocity Dynamics
- **JUCE Class:** Inline in voice/exciters.
- **Purpose:** Harder playing brightens/strengthens the excitation — the model's dynamic response (FUNC-06).
- **Parameters Affected:** `velToBrightness`, velocity (from MIDI note-on).
- **Configuration:** velocity scales exciter amplitude AND raises exciter LPF cutoff; depth = `velToBrightness`.

### 12. Amp Envelope + Output
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::ADSR` (attack/release dominant) + `juce::SmoothedValue<float>` output gain.
- **Purpose:** Output amplitude shaping (mainly attack/release — the body's decay is intrinsic to the resonator; matters most for sustained Bow). Voice lifetime gates on this envelope.
- **Parameters Affected:** `ampAttack`, `ampRelease`, `outputLevel`.
- **Configuration:** A ≈ 0.001–2 s, R ≈ 0–5 s. `outputLevel` dB→linear, 20 ms smoothed.

### 13. Visualization Analyzer (lock-free taps)
- **JUCE Class:** O-simpleFM `VizRing` (8192-sample lock-free overwrite ring) + message-thread `juce::dsp::FFT` (4096, Blackman-Harris) + relaxed atomics for loop-energy & modal-stem snapshots. Near-verbatim reuse of `FmVizAnalyzer.h`.
- **Purpose:** Feeds the four headline visuals (loop/flow diagram, scope, spectrum, modal stems) from the ACTUAL loop state of the lead voice (UI-02/03/04/05).
- **Parameters Affected:** none (read-only tap).
- **Configuration:** Audio thread COPY-ONLY into the ring + atomic writes (PERF-01: no alloc/lock/FFT on audio thread). FFT + downsample on the editor's 30 Hz Timer.

## Processing Chain

```
                MIDI note-on (note, velocity)  ─────────────┐
                                                             ▼
  ┌──────────────────────── PER VOICE (×16, juce::Synthesiser) ───────────────────────┐
  │                                                                                    │
  │   EXCITATION  (one of, by excitationType)                                          │
  │     Pluck  → filtered noise burst ─┐                                               │
  │     Strike → band-limited impulse ─┼─► [position comb] ─► exciter sample e[n]      │
  │     Bow    → friction drive ───────┘   (velocity → amp + brightness)               │
  │                                                                                    │
  │                         e[n]                                                       │
  │                          ▼                                                         │
  │   RESONATOR  (by resonatorType)                                                    │
  │     ┌─ STRING (Karplus-Strong)                                                     │
  │     │     delay.push(feedback·loopLPF(out) + e[n]);  out = delay.pop()             │
  │     │       ▲ Thiran fractional delay (TUNING)   ▲ loopLPF=Damping  ▲ feedback=Decay│
  │     │       └──────────────── feedback loop ─────┴──────────────────┘             │
  │     │     [nice: Waveguide = dual Thiran rails + bridge/nut reflect]               │
  │     └─ MODAL  (8 resonant bandpass biquads in parallel, driven by e[n])            │
  │           f_k = f0·k·√(1+B·k²)  (Inharmonicity=B);  Q_k,gain_k (ModeBrightness)    │
  │                          ▼                                                         │
  │                      resonator out r[n]                                            │
  │                          ▼                                                         │
  │   MATERIAL/DAMPING already applied inside loop (String) / per-mode gain (Modal)    │
  │     Material macro co-moves Damping (loop LPF) + Decay (feedback)                  │
  │                          ▼                                                         │
  │   AMP ENVELOPE (ADSR, attack/release) ── voice lifetime gate                       │
  │                          ▼                                                         │
  └──────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                             ▼  (Σ voices)
                       Output gain (outputLevel, smoothed)
                             ▼
                    ┌─► VizRing (lock-free, lead voice) ─► message-thread FFT/scope/stems
                    ▼
                  Audio out (stereo: mono voice summed → L=R)
```

**Routing notes:**
- The **String** path contains the one intentional **feedback loop** (the KS loop). It is the headline visual (energy circulating + dampening each pass).
- The **Modal** path is **feed-forward** (parallel resonant filters) — no loop, no stability risk (O-Bassoon: modal banks are CPU/stability-predictable).
- `excitationType` selects the exciter; `resonatorType` selects String vs Modal — both exciter and resonator are independent switches, so any exciter drives any resonator (FUNC-04).
- Position: v1.0 → comb on the exciter (KS); `nice` → true rail-split injection (Waveguide).
- Viz taps the **lead voice** loop state only.

## System Architecture

### MIDI Routing

**Input handling:** Standard polyphonic MIDI note-in (`juce::Synthesiser` / `SynthesiserVoice`), omni. `IS_SYNTH TRUE`, `NEEDS_MIDI_INPUT TRUE`.

**Note mapping:**
- Note-on → allocate voice; pitch = `getMidiNoteInHertz(note)` × tune; velocity (0–127→0–1) → exciter strength + brightness (`velToBrightness`).
- Note-off → Bow drive stops; String/Modal ring out under the amp release; voice freed when amp envelope + resonator energy fall below threshold.
- No CC/MPE/aftertouch mapping in v1.0 (out of scope — only velocity→brightness).

**JUCE classes:** `juce::Synthesiser`, `juce::SynthesiserVoice`, `juce::SynthesiserSound`, `juce::MidiBuffer`, `juce::MidiMessage`. On-screen WebView keyboard (optional, Stage 3) via `juce::MidiMessageCollector` (O-simpleFM `handleUiMidi` pattern).

### State Persistence

**What is saved:** All 17 APVTS parameters (automatic via `AudioProcessorValueTreeState`). No non-parameter custom state (no file paths, no folders). Factory presets are code (`FactoryPresets.cpp`, O-simpleFM pattern), not embedded binary.

**JUCE classes:** `AudioProcessorValueTreeState::state` → `getStateInformation` / `setStateInformation` (XML via ValueTree). Standard sibling pattern.

### File I/O — none. Multi-output — none (stereo out only).

## Algorithm Details

### Karplus-Strong loop (String)
**Algorithm:** `e[n]` written into delay at trigger; per sample `out = delay.popSample(ch, frac); s = loopLPF(out); delay.pushSample(ch, g·s + e_sustain[n])`. For Pluck/Strike `e_sustain` is zero after the burst (energy circulates); for Bow it is the continuous friction injection.
**Implementation notes:** Thiran fractional delay for tuning; group-delay compensation in `N`; `g` clamped `[0.80,0.999]`; crossfade loop-LPF coeff changes over 64 samples; DC-block output.

### Modal resonant bank (Modal)
**Algorithm:** 8 parallel 2nd-order bandpass biquads (RBJ constant-skirt) excited by `e[n]`; `f_k = f0·k·√(1+B·k²)`, `Q_k` from per-mode T60, output `Σ gain_k · bp_k(e[n])`.
**Implementation notes:** Custom direct-form Df1 arrays (per O-Bassoon — avoid `juce::dsp::IIR::Filter` ProcessSpec/AudioBlock overhead at 128 instances); block-rate coefficient recompute; `epsilon` guards; band-rate `gain_k` from `modeBrightness` tilt.

### Bow friction (Bow exciter)
**Algorithm (String):** memoryless STK bow table — `v_delta = v_bow − v_string_junction`; friction `f(v_delta)` (sharp near zero = stick, drops off = slip); inject `f·bowForce` into the junction. **(Modal):** sustained band-limited friction noise scaled by `bowForce`.
**Implementation notes:** memoryless tier ONLY (highest-risk component — validate basic sustained tone before any enhancement); clamp output; `sqrt`/division epsilon guards (O-Reed pattern).

### Inharmonicity / Material macro / Velocity
See Core Components 6, 10, 11 and Open Questions 2, 3 above.

---

## Integration Points

### Feature Dependencies
- **Exciter → Resonator:** the exciter sample `e[n]` is the resonator input; both resonators consume the SAME `e[n]` (FUNC-04 cross-driving falls out for free).
- **Tuning → Damping:** loop-LPF cutoff (Damping) changes the loop group delay → tuning compensation must read the current cutoff (String only).
- **Material macro → Damping + Decay:** writes both parameter values; must run before the loop reads them.
- **Lead-voice tracker → Viz:** the most-recently-triggered voice publishes loop-energy + modal-stem snapshots; everything else is silent to the viz.
- **Resonator switch → exciter behavior:** Bow injection differs (junction drive for String vs noise drive for Modal); Position uses comb (String) vs rail-split (Waveguide).

### Parameter Interactions
- `damping` + `decay` jointly set perceived material; `material` macro is a convenience over them (it writes them).
- `decay` near max + Bow continuous injection: bounded because `g<1` is hard-clamped AND the Bow friction is saturating/clamped (no runaway — QUAL-01).
- `inharmonicity`/`modeBrightness` are no-ops in String mode; `stringModel`/`excitationPosition`-as-pickup are no-ops in Modal mode (UI greys these per resonator).
- `velToBrightness` scales how much velocity moves exciter amplitude + cutoff (shared across all three exciters).

### Processing Order (per sample, per voice)
1. Compute exciter sample `e[n]` (Pluck/Strike: burst then 0; Bow: continuous friction).
2. Apply position comb to `e[n]` (KS) — Waveguide injects at rail split instead.
3. Resonator: String KS loop (pop → loopLPF → push `g·s + e`) OR Modal bank (`Σ gain_k·bp_k(e)`).
4. Apply amp envelope; accumulate into voice output.
5. (Lead voice only) publish loop-energy scalar / modal-stem array.
6. Σ voices → output gain → audio out + VizRing copy.

**Parallel:** all 16 voices are independent (no inter-voice state). Modal modes within a voice are parallel.

### Thread Boundaries
- **Audio thread:** all DSP in `processBlock`; parameter reads via `getRawParameterValue()->load()`; VizRing writes + atomic snapshot writes (copy-only, no alloc/lock — PERF-01).
- **Message thread:** APVTS writes from WebView; FFT/scope/stem computation on the editor Timer (30 Hz); preset load/save; Material-macro→Damping/Decay parameter writes (UI-driven, atomic via APVTS).
- **No background thread** (no file I/O).
- **Communication:** APVTS atomics; `VizRing` lock-free ring; relaxed `std::atomic` for loop-energy scalar, modal-stem array (fixed-size), and lead-voice pitch.

## Implementation Risks

### Bow Friction Drive
**Complexity:** HIGH · **Risk Level:** HIGH
**Risk factors:** friction stick-slip is the classic instability source (blow-up, screech, NaN); must sustain without runaway; must read musical across the keyboard; interacts with the String feedback loop.
**Alternative approaches:** (1) Memoryless STK bow table (chosen core); (2) sustained filtered-noise drive (simplest, less "bowed" but stable); (3) elasto-plastic / thermal friction (O-Bowed enhanced tier — OUT OF SCOPE).
**Fallback architecture:** If the memoryless bow table reads poorly or destabilizes the KS loop → fall back to **sustained filtered friction-noise into the loop** (still satisfies "Bow sustains"), accept a less idiomatic bow timbre.
**Mitigation:** Implement memoryless-first and validate a basic sustained bowed tone BEFORE any refinement (O-Bowed memory). Hard-clamp friction output; epsilon-guard divisions; render-harness asserts bounded/finite at max Bow Force + max Decay.

### Karplus-Strong Tuning Accuracy
**Complexity:** MEDIUM · **Risk Level:** MEDIUM
**Risk factors:** loop-filter group delay + all-pass phase delay shift pitch; high notes (short delays) most sensitive; the loop comb confounds naive spectral pitch probes.
**Alternative approaches:** (1) Thiran all-pass + group-delay compensation (chosen, O-Lyrica/O-Bowed validated); (2) Lagrange3rd interpolation (smoother under modulation but a different phase-delay model — unneeded, no glide).
**Fallback architecture:** If Thiran compensation drifts at the top octave → add a small per-note tuning-table correction measured offline by the harness.
**Mitigation:** **Stage-2 gate = single-note AUTOCORRELATION pitch probe** in the render-harness (NOT a single-bin DFT — the KS comb fools spectral probes; this mirrors the O-simpleGrain granular-pitch finding). Assert measured f0 within a few cents at C1, C3, C5, C7.

### Modal Resonator Bank
**Complexity:** MEDIUM · **Risk Level:** LOW
**Risk factors:** 128 biquads (8×16) coefficient cost; high-Q stability; inharmonicity readout matching audible stems.
**Alternative approaches:** (1) Custom direct-form biquad bank (chosen, O-Bassoon precedent); (2) O-Bells triggered decaying-sinusoid oscillators (rejected — doesn't respond to a continuous/arbitrary exciter, breaks FUNC-04 cross-driving).
**Fallback architecture:** Reduce mode count 8→6 if CPU-bound (unlikely).
**Mitigation:** Block-rate coefficient recompute; clamp Q; reuse O-Bells ratio/decay tables; stem display reads the SAME `f_k`/amplitudes the audio uses (truthful by construction).

### Waveguide String (`nice`)
**Complexity:** MEDIUM · **Risk Level:** LOW (deferrable)
**Risk factors:** dual-rail group-delay bookkeeping; only needed for "true" Position.
**Fallback architecture:** Ship KS only for v1.0; Position via exciter comb. Waveguide is a pure add-on phase reusing O-Lyrica/O-Bowed `WaveguideString`.
**Mitigation:** Keep `stringModel` a choice param wired from Stage 1; if Waveguide slips, the choice exposes KS only — no contract break.

### Real-time-safe Visualization
**Complexity:** LOW · **Risk Level:** LOW
**Mitigation:** Verbatim O-simpleFM `VizRing`/`FmVizAnalyzer` (already pluginval-clean); audio thread copy-only.

### Overall Project Risk
**Overall complexity:** HIGH (two resonator engines + three exciters; one HIGH-risk friction component). **Highest risk:** Bow friction (~50% of project risk). **Recommended approach:** KS + Pluck first (validate tuning + material), then Strike/Bow + dynamics, then Modal + cross-drive, then (nice) Waveguide — exactly the Stage-2 phase order in ROADMAP.md.

---

## Architecture Decisions

### Modal = resonant filter bank, NOT triggered decaying sinusoids
**Decision:** Drive the modal body with a parallel **resonant bandpass biquad bank** fed the exciter signal.
**Rationale:** The unifying pedagogy is "excitation DRIVES a resonator." A filter bank rings from ANY input (impulse, noise burst, sustained friction), so the same three exciters drive Modal exactly as they drive String (FUNC-04). O-Bells' triggered sinusoid-bank is a strike-only shortcut.
**Alternatives considered:** O-Bells triggered decaying oscillators (rejected — not exciter-driven, breaks cross-driving); `juce::dsp::IIR::Filter` bank (rejected — ProcessSpec/AudioBlock overhead at 128 instances, O-Bassoon).
**Tradeoffs accepted:** Slightly more per-mode math vs a phase accumulator; acceptable because it makes the model honest and is cheap (O-Bassoon validated 128 biquads).

### KS string is the v1.0 String engine; Waveguide is `nice`
**Decision:** Ship single-delay Karplus-Strong; realise Position via exciter comb; make the dual-rail Waveguide an optional Stage-2 phase.
**Rationale:** KS is the canonical algorithm the class derives, the simplest truthful String, and the one the headline loop diagram visualizes. Position-as-comb is the O-Lyrica `PluckExciter` approach — gives Position meaning without the rails.
**Alternatives considered:** Waveguide-only (rejected — heavier, the loop diagram is muddier than the single KS loop the class draws). **Tradeoffs:** v1.0 Position is spectral (comb) not a true pickup; full pickup arrives with the Waveguide nice-tier.

### Thiran all-pass for fractional delay
**Decision:** `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float, Thiran>` for the loop delay.
**Rationale:** Thiran 1st-order is an all-pass fractional delay (flat magnitude — critical so loop damping comes ONLY from the explicit Damping LPF, not the interpolator); validated in O-Bowed; satisfies DSP-02's "all-pass interpolation" literally.
**Alternatives considered:** Lagrange3rd (O-Lyrica — fine but a different phase-delay model; chosen by O-Lyrica because it modulates pitch for glissando, which v1.0 lacks). **Tradeoffs:** Thiran is unsuitable for fast delay modulation — fine here since pitch is fixed per note.

### Single global lead-voice viz tap
**Decision:** One viz tap follows the most-recently-triggered voice.
**Rationale:** The pedagogy is ONE readable model; per-voice viz is noisy and costly. Mirrors O-simpleSubtractive's lead-voice display.
**Tradeoffs:** Chords show only the lead voice's loop/stems — acceptable and clearer for teaching.

---

## Special Considerations

### Thread Safety
- All param reads atomic (`getRawParameterValue()->load()`); coefficient updates happen on the audio thread (no allocations), crossfaded to avoid clicks.
- Viz: `VizRing` lock-free ring + relaxed atomics for the loop-energy scalar, the fixed-size modal-stem array, and lead-voice pitch. No locks on the audio thread.
- Material macro writes `damping`/`decay` via APVTS on the message thread (atomic).

### Performance
- KS String voice: ~1 delay + 1 one-pole + a few mults → very cheap (<1% per voice).
- Modal voice: 8 biquads → cheap; 16 voices × 8 = 128 biquads, O-Bassoon-validated affordable.
- Bow friction: a table lookup + clamp per sample → cheap.
- Estimated total: well under 20% single core at 48 kHz, 16 voices. No oversampling needed (KS loop LPF + band-limited exciters keep HF bounded; revisit only if the Strike impulse aliases at the top octave — the harness audits this).

### Denormal Protection
- `juce::ScopedNoDenormals` in `processBlock`. Loop feedback `g<1` plus DC-blocker prevent denormal/DC accumulation; modal biquads epsilon-guarded.

### Sample Rate Handling
- `prepareToPlay`: size delay lines for lowest expected note at highest rate (covers ~20 Hz @ 192 kHz, O-Lyrica `MAX_COMB_DELAY 8192`); recompute all cutoffs/coeffs; reset `VizRing` not required (fixed alloc).
- Delay length, biquad coeffs, feedback-from-decay, group-delay comp all sample-rate dependent → recomputed in `prepareToPlay` and on note-on.

### Latency
- Zero reported latency (no lookahead, no oversampling in v1.0). `getLatencySamples()` stays 0 (use `setLatencySamples(0)` — getter is non-virtual in JUCE 8). `getTailLengthSeconds()` ≈ 5 s (max amp release / ring-out).

## Research References

### Professional Plugins (from BRIEF — context, not re-researched)
1. **Yamaha VL1** — first commercial waveguide instrument; the historical anchor for String/Waveguide.
2. **Logic Sculpture / Ableton Tension + Collision + Corpus** — modern string + modal (exciter→resonator→material is exactly their mental model); O-simplePhysicalModelSynth is the minimal teaching counterpart.
3. **AAS Chromaphone / String Studio** — commercial modal + string; reference for the Material macro and mode behavior.
4. **Madrona Aalto / Kaivo** — patchable physical models; reference for the gesture→visible-consequence ethos.

### In-house References (PRIMARY — validated, in-repo, JUCE 8.0.9)
- **O-Lyrica** `Source/DSP/WaveguideString.h`, `PluckExciter.h` — KS/waveguide loop, `OnePoleLPF`, fractional-delay tuning, group-delay compensation, position comb, feedback-from-decay-time, shadow-filter crossfade. **Direct reuse.**
- **O-Bells** `Source/BellVoice.h` — modal partial bank, harmonic/bell/gamelan ratio tables, `DECAY_MULTIPLIERS`, `StrikeExciter`, per-mode freq/amp/decay. **Direct reuse for Modal + Strike.**
- **O-Bowed** `Source/DSP/WaveguideString.h`, `BowedStringVoice` — dual Thiran rails, bridge loss filter, memoryless friction junction. **Reference for Bow + Waveguide.**
- **O-simpleFM** `Source/FmVizAnalyzer.h`, `PluginProcessor.h`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `tests/render-harness/main.cpp` — `VizRing` lock-free viz, 16-voice `juce::Synthesiser` structure, APVTS ParamIDs namespace, WebView2 CMake flags, offline render-harness gate (adapt DFT→autocorrelation for KS tuning). **Structural template.**
- **O-simpleAdditive / O-simpleSubtractive** — pedagogical sibling structure: irreducible control set, concept-isolating presets, tooltip approach, lead-voice display tap.

### JUCE Classes
- `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float, Thiran>` — all-pass fractional delay (loop tuning).
- Custom `OnePoleLPF` (bilinear) — loop damping (O-Lyrica POD pattern; trivially snapshotted for crossfade).
- Custom direct-form biquad bank — modal resonators (O-Bassoon precedent; NOT `juce::dsp::IIR::Filter` at scale).
- `juce::ADSR`, `juce::Random` — exciters + amp envelope.
- `juce::Synthesiser` / `SynthesiserVoice` (16 voices), `juce::MidiMessageCollector` (WebView keyboard).
- `juce::dsp::FFT` + `juce::dsp::WindowingFunction` — message-thread spectrum (4096 Blackman-Harris).
- `juce::AudioProcessorValueTreeState` — params + state.

### Technical Resources
- Karplus & Strong (1983), *Digital Synthesis of Plucked-String and Drum Timbres*.
- Julius O. Smith, *Physical Audio Signal Processing* (CCRMA) — waveguide + modal theory; Thiran all-pass tuning (Jaffe-Smith KS extension).
- Fletcher & Rossing, *The Physics of Musical Instruments* — inharmonicity `f_k = f0·k·√(1+B·k²)`.
- STK (Cook/Scavone) — `BowTable` memoryless friction reference.

## Notes

- **Naming gotchas (binding for Stage 2):** name voice classes `StringVoice` / `ModalVoice` (or one `PhysicalModelVoice` with a resonator switch) — NEVER `SamplerVoice`/`SamplerSound` (shadows `juce::` types). Avoid bare `end`/`begin` APVTS param-ID C++ symbols under `using namespace ...ParamIDs`.
- **CMake (binding):** `IS_SYNTH TRUE`, `NEEDS_MIDI_INPUT TRUE`, `NEEDS_WEB_BROWSER TRUE`, `NEEDS_WEBVIEW2 TRUE`, `JUCE_USE_WIN_WEBVIEW2_WITH_STATIC_LINKING=1` (COMPAT-02). Only ONE `juce_add_binary_data` target (WebView UI) → no namespace-collision risk; if embedded presets are ever added as binary data, give the 2nd target a DISTINCT `NAMESPACE`.
- **Render-harness (binding):** Stage-2 correctness gate is an offline console app (no DAW). For KS/waveguide tuning use a single-note **autocorrelation** pitch probe (loop comb confounds spectral probes). Compile under `JUCE_WEB_BROWSER=0` and DROP `PluginEditor.cpp` from harness sources so the Stage-3 WebView editor doesn't break the harness; guard `createEditor` with `#if JUCE_WEB_BROWSER`. Re-run the harness at the START of Stage 4.
- **Open future work (v1.1+, out of scope):** Blow/tube resonator; Bow Speed control; true Waveguide pickup if it slips from v1.0; larger modal preset library.
